Review date: 2026-07-31. Package version reviewed: TaxaExpect 0.1.0. Review conducted by
Claude Code, using the template in `inst/Code and Domain Review 2.Rmd`. This is TaxaExpect's
first full review of this kind -- every sibling package in the ecosystem (TaxaTools,
TaxaFetch, TaxaMatch, TaxaLikely) already had one; this closes that gap. Findings and fixes
are combined in one pass (no separate response document), following the `taxafetch_review.Rmd`
precedent: a background research pass read every R file against the template and reported
candidate findings; every High-severity claim below was then independently re-verified against
the actual running code (live R execution, not re-reading the report) before being trusted or
fixed -- several were confirmed exactly as reported, none were found to be false positives at
the High tier.

`devtools::check()`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes. `devtools::test()`: 538 expectations (up
from 536 before this review -- two pre-existing tests that directly encoded the old, buggy
`.safe_normalise()` behavior as their expected result were rewritten to assert the corrected
behavior instead, net +2 assertions), 0 failures (37 warnings, all pre-existing and benign: a
`glmmTMB`/`TMB` package-version-mismatch environment warning repeated per test file, plus tests
that deliberately capture convergence warnings). `lintr::lint_package()`: no `.lintr` existed
before this review (every sibling package has one); one was added (line length 120, UTF-8,
matching the ecosystem convention) and most real findings fixed -- see the Coding standards
section below for what remains open and why.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Code Review

Purpose: To produce high quality code that is well written and organized according to
best coding practices.

### [x] Functionality: The code is readable, organized, and efficient. Six real bugs fixed.

Overall organization is consistent with the rest of the ecosystem (roxygen throughout,
`.`-prefixed internal helpers, `package::function()` cross-package calls). Six real
correctness bugs were found and fixed, all confirmed by direct live execution before
touching any code -- listed here because they are functionality bugs (silent wrong output
or a broken invariant), not style:

**`compute_moran_basis.R` -- `eigen(M, symmetric = TRUE)` silently wrong on any real,
irregular grid (High, fixed).** The Moran operator `M` was built from a row-standardised
adjacency matrix (`W_std <- W / row_sums`), which is asymmetric for any grid where two
cells have different neighbour counts -- true for essentially every real, non-toroidal
grid (confirmed live with a 5-node unequal-degree graph: max asymmetry 0.33, not a
rounding artifact). `eigen(..., symmetric = TRUE)` silently reads only the lower
triangle of an asymmetric input with **no error or warning**, producing a completely
different set of eigenvalues, signs, and eigenvectors than the correct general
eigendecomposition (confirmed live: `[0.789, 0.073, -0.270, -0.501, -1.091]` vs. the
correct `[-0.857, 0.654, -0.5, -0.297, 0]`). The wrong `B1...Bk` spatial basis columns
then feed directly into `train_biodiversity_model()`/`generate_full_priors()` for any
caller using `moran_k > 0` -- `build_priors()`'s own default. Fixed: `M` is now built
from the underlying binary adjacency matrix `W` directly (already symmetric by
construction, from a symmetric distance test) instead of its row-standardised form --
the row-standardisation step was removed entirely, not patched. Roxygen `@details`
corrected to state the symmetry requirement explicitly.

**`generate_full_priors.R` -- phi cap never fires on the package's own recommended
formula (High, fixed).** The "principled" phi (Beta-prior effective sample size) cap,
documented as being derived from the model's own `taxon_name:grid_id` random-effect
variance, looked up `glmmTMB::VarCorr(...)$cond[["taxon_name.grid_id"]]` -- a period,
not the colon glmmTMB actually uses (confirmed live against a real fitted glmmTMB model:
`names(VarCorr(m)$cond)` returns `"taxon_name:grid_id"`). The lookup therefore always
returned `NULL`, silently falling through to the hardcoded `max_phi = 1000` fallback on
every single call using the package's own documented recommended formula
(`... + (1 | taxon_name:grid_id)`, `TaxaExpect/CLAUDE.md`'s own "Recommended formula").
Where the real grid-level variance implies a materially tighter cap, this could produce
falsely narrow (overconfident) Beta priors. Fixed: one-character fix (`.` -> `:`),
confirmed live that `as.numeric(mat)` now correctly extracts the scalar variance.

**`prepare_model_dataframe.R`/`train_biodiversity_model_by_group.R` --
`sampling_group_col` silently drops every NA-grouped row (High, fixed in both files).**
Base R's `split(data, data[[col]])` silently omits rows whose grouping value is `NA`
(confirmed live: `split(1:5, c("a","a",NA,"b","b"))` returns only 4 of 5 elements, with
no warning). Any taxon whose `sampling_group_col` value is unclassified therefore
vanished entirely from the grouped output of both functions, undermining the whole
point of the Session 149 group-aware effort-denominator feature (enforcing the "shared
effort assumption"). `train_biodiversity_model_by_group()` additionally used
`sort(unique(...))` to enumerate groups, which also silently drops NA (`sort()`'s
default `na.last = NA`). Fixed in both files: NA is now kept as its own explicit group
(`sampling_group = NA`) via `factor(x, exclude = NULL)` before splitting, with a
`message()` reporting the affected row count. Indexing was switched from by-name to
by-position throughout both files, since `list[[NA]]` returns `NULL` rather than the
actual NA-named element (confirmed live) -- the exact list-indexing footgun this
package's own `compute_adaptive_sampling_groups.R` had already independently worked
around; that file was the correct reference pattern, not an inconsistency to resolve
the other way.

**`prepare_model_dataframe.R` -- `scale_params` attribute silently kept only the first
group's values (High, fixed).** `dplyr::bind_rows()` on a list of data frames each
carrying a custom `scale_params` attribute keeps only the FIRST element's attribute
value, discarding every other group's (confirmed live with a two-group toy
reproduction). Any group after the first therefore had its covariate center/scale
silently replaced by the first group's, for any caller consuming
`prepare_model_dataframe(sampling_group_col = ...)`'s combined output directly (a
documented, standalone capability -- `train_biodiversity_model_by_group()` itself
sidesteps this by re-deriving its own per-group `scale_params` internally, per its own
existing session notes, but did not fix the underlying attribute-loss bug in the
function it wraps). Fixed: the combined output no longer carries a flat `scale_params`
attribute when grouped; it carries `scale_params_by_group`, a named list of per-group
`scale_params` lists, documented in the function's own `@return`.

**`create_sites_from_grid.R` -- `grid_id` silently collides distinct cells for any
`grid_size < 0.1` (High, fixed).** `grid_id` was always formatted via a fixed
`sprintf("Grid_%.1f_%.1f", ...)`, regardless of `grid_size`. For any finer resolution
(a real, supported choice -- `optimize_grid_size()` can legitimately recommend one),
two genuinely distinct cells collide into one label (confirmed live: `grid_size = 0.05`
rounds `34.05` and `34.10` to the same `"34.1"` string), silently pooling spatially
distinct sites into one `taxon_name:grid_id` random-effect level with no warning. Fixed:
decimal precision is now derived from `grid_size` itself (`max(1L, -floor(log10(grid_size)))`),
preserving the previous 1-decimal-place output exactly for `grid_size >= 0.1`.

**`optimize_grid_size.R` -- two related bugs in resolution scoring/selection (High and
Medium-High, both fixed).** (1) `.safe_normalise()` masked `+Inf`/`-Inf` inputs to `NA`
before computing the normalisation range, but never restored them afterward -- a
resolution with the theoretically BEST possible stability score (`cv_N == 0`, perfectly
uniform sampling effort, a realistic case for structured survey designs) ended up with
`NA` instead of the correct `1`, which then propagates through the composite score and
sorts last via `arrange(desc(...))`, silently disqualifying that resolution from ever
being selected as `best_grid`. Fixed: `+Inf`/`-Inf` inputs are now explicitly restored
to `1`/`0` after normalisation. (2) Fallback C's `single_grid_size`, documented to
guarantee "all observations pooled into one site," is not actually guaranteed by its
formula for an arbitrary bbox position -- confirmed live with a concrete counterexample
(bbox `[10.0, 12.3]`, span 2.3: the formula's `single_grid_size = 2.36` still produced
two distinct grid cells, `9.44` and `11.8`, contradicting the fallback's own printed
message). Fixed: the grid size is now verified against the real coordinates and grown
(geometric, capped at 20 iterations) until it demonstrably collapses to one cell for
the actual data at hand, rather than trusting an unverified closed-form formula for an
arbitrary bbox alignment.

### [x] Optimizations: No significant inefficiencies found beyond the correctness issues above.

No algorithmic complexity concerns. `compute_moran_basis()`'s fix is a net simplification
(one fewer matrix operation, not an added cost).

### [x] Coding standards: Docstrings/comments checked against actual behavior; several
gaps found and fixed; `.lintr` added, most findings fixed, remainder documented below.

Multiple doc-vs-code mismatches were found (beyond the ones already listed above as
functionality bugs, since fixing the code made the docs correct automatically):

- `train_biodiversity_model.R`'s Tier 2 empirical fallback (`tier2_empirical`, used when
  the Tier 2 GLMM fails to fit) computed `theta_mean_emp`/`theta_sd_emp` only over rows
  where `n_species > 0` -- a conditional "typical rate given detected," not the marginal
  prevalence rate the roxygen implies ("observed mean/SD theta"). Systematically
  inflated, worst for a rare species detected at only 1-2 of many surveyed sites. Fixed
  to average over ALL surveyed rows for a detected taxon x habitat combo (including the
  zero-detection rows `prepare_model_dataframe()` zero-fills), while still restricting
  output rows to combos observed at least once (so `observed_in_habitat` downstream
  logic, which reads this table's taxon/habitat combos, is unaffected).
- `screen_spatial_formula.R`'s `sd_threshold` was documented as a "coefficient of
  variation," a self-contradictory phrase ("CV... on the logit scale") since the code
  never divides by a mean anywhere -- it's compared directly against each random
  slope's absolute fitted SD. Doc-only fix.
- `train_biodiversity_model.R`'s `full_data` parameter silently changes what "singleton"
  means: a raw-record count when supplied, an occupied-grid-cell count when omitted (the
  default) -- a species with 3 clustered raw records at one cell is a singleton under the
  default path but not under the `full_data` path. Not previously disclosed. Doc-only fix.
- `train_biodiversity_model_by_group.R`'s exported name (34 characters) exceeds the
  30-character `object_length_linter` convention -- flagged, not renamed (a real API
  break for a name already referenced throughout `CLAUDE.md`'s Function Inventory and
  several session notes, for cosmetic gain only); recorded as a `.lintr` exclusion
  instead.
- `recover_demoted_species.R`'s `rank_system` parameter was declared and documented but
  never referenced in the function body -- genuinely dead (internal, `@noRd`, single
  call site in `build_priors.R`). Removed entirely (not deprecated) rather than left as
  misleading documentation, since it is unexported and has exactly one caller, updated
  in the same pass.
- `TaxaExpect-package.R`'s package-level roxygen index omitted several newer exported
  functions (`prepare_model_dataframe`, `train_biodiversity_model_by_group`,
  `compute_adaptive_sampling_groups`, `compute_moran_basis`, `screen_spatial_formula`,
  `add_pca_covariates`, `generate_domestic_food_priors`,
  `plot_theta_map_interactive`). Fixed -- all now listed.
- `create_sites_from_grid.R`'s own `@return` example had latitude and longitude swapped
  in its prose ("lat = -119.5, lon = 34.0" -- backwards for a Southern California
  example, though internally consistent with the example's own output string). Fixed.

`.lintr` added (line length 120, UTF-8, matching every sibling package). Real findings
fixed: two `else`-on-own-line `brace_linter` hits, three `spaces_inside_linter` hits
(`x[[ y ]]` -> `x[[y]]`), three `return_linter` hits (explicit `return()` at a function's
final statement), two `sapply(x, function(y) ...)`-without-braces `brace_linter` hits, one
compound-semicolon test-file statement split across lines, comma-spacing in one test
fixture, and one over-long `message()` string split via `paste0()`-equivalent multi-arg
`message()` (safe here, unlike `sprintf()` -- see this package's own Known Footguns entry
on the split-string `sprintf()` bug; `message()`'s `...` genuinely concatenates, confirmed
before relying on it).

**Not fixed this pass, left as documented `.lintr` exclusions or open items:** roughly 40
remaining `object_name_linter` hits on short, conventional statistical/matrix notation
(`W`, `I`, `M`, `N_total`, `min_N_threshold` -- used consistently throughout this package's
spatial-modelling code, matching standard notation in the cited MEM/PCNM literature) and a
handful of long `message()`/`stop()` strings exceeding 120 characters. Both are cosmetic-only
with no correctness implication; renaming ~15 short single-letter matrix variables used
throughout `compute_moran_basis.R` would touch every line of that function for no behavior
change and was judged not worth the risk this session, unlike the sibling packages' own
lintr passes which dealt with a much smaller residual after their own object-name findings.
Left open rather than silently claimed clean.

### [x] Automated tests: Confirmed passing when run locally after all fixes above.

`devtools::test()`: 538 expectations, 0 failures. Two pre-existing tests in
`test-optimize_grid_size.R` directly asserted the OLD, buggy `.safe_normalise()` behavior
(`is.na(out[3])` for an `Inf` input, `all(is.na(out))` for an all-non-finite input) --
these were rewritten to assert the corrected behavior (`Inf` -> `1`, `-Inf` -> `0`,
bare `NA` stays `NA`) rather than left broken or silently reverted.

### [x] Vulnerabilities: None found requiring a fix.

This package has no direct network I/O, file-path construction from untrusted input, or
`eval`/`parse` of external data -- all external data acquisition (GBIF, NCBI, LLM calls)
is delegated to TaxaFetch/TaxaHabitat/TaxaTools, already reviewed separately
(`taxafetch_review.Rmd` found and fixed a real SSRF gap there). `generate_domestic_food_priors.R`
(the largest, newest file, checked most closely for this reason) calls
`TaxaFetch::fetch_inat_occurrences()`/`TaxaTools::clean_taxon_names()` but does not itself
construct URLs, file paths, or shell commands from any input. `plot_theta_map_interactive.R`'s
`.he()` HTML-escaping helper (for Leaflet popup content) escaped `&`/`<`/`>`/`"` but not `'`,
an incomplete escaping boundary against its own stated purpose -- fixed (added), though real
exposure was low (a single-user local interactive Shiny gadget, self-XSS at worst, not a
network-facing surface).

# Domain Review

Purpose: To ensure the code produces outputs, data, interfaces, or software that is
biologically reasonable when compared to other similar information available.

### [x] Scientific Rigor: Two real statistical bugs found and fixed (see Code Review above
for the full technical detail: `compute_moran_basis.R`'s asymmetric-eigendecomposition bug
and `train_biodiversity_model.R`'s Tier 2 conditional-vs-marginal-rate bug). Both directly
affect the numeric values TaxaExpect produces, not just crash behavior. One further
domain-specific finding, fixed:

**`generate_domestic_food_priors.R` -- `"x Triticosecale"` default entry silently never
survives name-cleaning (Medium, fixed).** Verified live against the real
`TaxaTools::clean_taxon_names()`: `"x Triticosecale"` (leading lowercase "x", standard
botanical hybrid notation for the wheat-rye hybrid crop) cleans to `NA` and is silently
dropped from the default `food_species_taxa` list every call -- confirmed distinct from
this list's other hybrid-formula entries (e.g. `"Citrus x aurantiifolia"`), which lossily
but successfully collapse to their genus. Fixed: corrected to the bare genus
`"Triticosecale"`, matching how this list already handles other genus-only entries.

### [x] Outputs: Comparable to expectation; one reporting-accuracy gap fixed.

**`report_priors.R` -- `n_grid_cells` inflated by 1 whenever `generate_domestic_food_priors()`
rows (which legitimately carry `grid_id = NA`) are present (Low, fixed).** `unique()` counts
`NA` as one more "distinct" value; the adjacent `n_taxa` computation three lines above
already correctly guards against the identical case, making this a genuine oversight rather
than a deliberate asymmetry. Fixed to match the existing `n_taxa` pattern -- relevant to
any Methods-text-quoted cell count once domestic/food priors are mixed into a report.

### [x] Algorithms: Appropriate for stated purpose, with the corrections above. One
additional real UI/data-integrity bug found and fixed in the interactive exploration tool:

**`plot_theta_map_interactive.R` -- `occ_sel()` uses `==` where its sibling reactive uses
`%in%` (Medium, fixed).** `occ[occ$taxon == input$taxon, ]` (vs. `pr_sel()`'s correct
`pr$taxon_name %in% input$taxon` two lines above) turns an NA in `occ$taxon` into an NA
logical mask entry, which `[`-indexing expands into a full ghost all-NA row -- a live
recurrence of the exact NA-comparison bug class this same file was already debugged for
once (2026-07-24 session, per `CLAUDE.md`; the earlier fix addressed a different reactive,
`taxon_name == input$taxon` matching undetected/singleton-mirror proxy rows, not this one).
Worse specifically when `occurrence_habitat_col = NULL` (a supported, documented mode),
since the habitat-filter step that happens to mask the ghost row in the default mode is
skipped. Fixed to `%in%`, matching the sibling reactive; the upstream `occ` construction
also gained an explicit `!is.na(occ$taxon)` filter alongside its existing lat/lon NA guard,
as defense in depth.

# File specific comments

- `R/compute_moran_basis.R` -- `M` now built from the symmetric binary `W` directly
  (row-standardisation step removed); `@details` corrected.
- `R/generate_full_priors.R` -- `grid_term` lookup key fixed (`.` -> `:`); two
  `spaces_inside_linter`/`return_linter` style fixes; `@importFrom dplyr` merged to one
  line (roxygen2 8.0.0 compatibility, see the note below).
- `R/prepare_model_dataframe.R` -- NA-drop and `scale_params`-attribute-loss both fixed
  in the `sampling_group_col` grouping path; `@return`/`@section` updated to document
  `scale_params_by_group`; `@importFrom dplyr` merged to one line.
- `R/train_biodiversity_model_by_group.R` -- matching NA-drop fix (positional indexing
  throughout).
- `R/create_sites_from_grid.R` -- `grid_id` decimal precision now derived from
  `grid_size`; `@return` example lat/lon corrected.
- `R/optimize_grid_size.R` -- `.safe_normalise()` Inf-restoration fix; Fallback C's
  `single_grid_size` now verified against real coordinates and grown until correct;
  `@importFrom dplyr` merged to one line.
- `R/train_biodiversity_model.R` -- Tier 2 empirical fallback now averages over all
  surveyed rows, not just detected ones; `@param full_data`'s singleton-definition gap
  documented; two `brace_linter`/one `spaces_inside_linter`/one `return_linter` style
  fixes; `@importFrom dplyr` merged to one line.
- `R/plot_theta_map_interactive.R` -- `occ_sel()`'s `==` -> `%in%`; upstream NA filter
  extended to `occ$taxon`.
- `R/generate_domestic_food_priors.R` -- `"x Triticosecale"` default corrected to
  `"Triticosecale"`.
- `R/report_priors.R` -- `n_grid_cells` NA-guard added, matching `n_taxa`'s existing
  pattern.
- `R/screen_spatial_formula.R` -- `sd_threshold` doc corrected (not a CV); two
  `sapply(...)`-without-braces fixes; one long `message()` split.
- `R/add_pca_covariates.R` -- explicit, actionable error added for missing values
  reaching `prcomp()` (previously an opaque low-level R error).
- `R/utils_plot.R` -- `.he()` gains apostrophe escaping.
- `R/recover_demoted_species.R` -- unused `rank_system` parameter removed; sole call
  site in `R/build_priors.R` updated to match.
- `R/TaxaExpect-package.R` -- package-level function index completed.
- 5 files (`prepare_model_dataframe.R`, `add_pca_covariates.R`,
  `plot_theta_map_interactive.R`, `compute_moran_basis.R`, `train_biodiversity_model.R`)
  had non-ASCII em-dash/multiplication/approx characters in comments and roxygen (no
  string literals affected) -- swept to ASCII equivalents, matching this ecosystem's
  established policy (every sibling package's own review did the same).
- `.lintr` added (new file); `.Rbuildignore` gained `^\.lintr$` (without it,
  `devtools::check()` produces a "hidden files" NOTE -- caught and fixed the same session,
  matching every sibling package's own `.Rbuildignore`).
- `tests/testthat/test-optimize_grid_size.R` -- the two `.safe_normalise()` tests that
  encoded the old buggy behavior rewritten to assert the fix (see Automated tests above).
- `tests/testthat/test-prepare_model_dataframe.R` / `test-generate_domestic_food_priors.R`
  -- minor lint fixes (comma spacing, compound-statement split), no behavior change.
- **Environment note, not a package bug:** this developer's current environment has
  roxygen2 8.0.0 installed against a `RoxygenNote: 7.3.3`-declared package (true for
  every package in this ecosystem, not specific to TaxaExpect). Version 8.0.0's stricter
  `@importFrom` parser rejects the multi-line-wrapped `@importFrom dplyr ...` blocks used
  throughout this package (and, unchanged, in every sibling package) -- `devtools::document()`
  errored on 4 of TaxaExpect's files until each was merged to one line (done this session,
  see the file list above). This is a real, currently-live blocker for regenerating any
  `.Rd` file in this package on this machine; it was not previously encountered because
  no prior session's edits happened to touch one of the affected roxygen blocks while also
  needing a `document()` run. Worth a `CLAUDE.md`-level note for future sessions (not added
  here, to keep this review scoped to TaxaExpect) if the same block is hit again in another
  package.
